summary: A property deal fell through at the last step. Not fraud, not a dispute: one co-owner had died without leaving a Will. Every year Indian families spend months, sometimes years, in court over assets that one document would have moved quietly. This one separates the three things almost everybody mixes up, a nominee, a legal heir and a Will, and walks through what actually happens to your money, investments and property after you are gone.

seo.title: Nominee vs Legal Heir vs Will, The Truth Every Indian Should Know
seo.description: A nominee is not the same as a legal heir, and neither is a Will. What actually happens to your money, property and investments in India.

takeaways.text: A nominee, a legal heir and a Will are three different things doing three different jobs, and assuming one covers the others is the mistake that starts most family disputes.
Indian families lose months and sometimes years in court over assets that one document would have transferred without an argument.
If you own a house, mutual funds, bank accounts, insurance, EPF or gold, every one of them needs an answer to the question of who gets it and how.
Dying without a Will does not mean nothing happens. It means succession law decides, and that may not match what you would have chosen.
This is one to act on rather than file away. The episode covers how to put a legally valid Will in place, and it is not a substitute for proper legal advice.
